newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada first to sign beef import deal with China.
newsitem.headline: Canada first to sign beef import deal with China.

text.p: Canada on Tuesday became the first nation to sign a beef import protocol with China, Canadian Agriculture Minister Ralph Goodale said.

"This protocal is not only the first that China has signed with Canada on beef, it is the first that China has signed with any country and demonstrates the high esteem in which Canada's animal and food hygiene system is held there," Goodale said.
The protocol sets the terms and conditions under which Canadian producers may export their beef products directly to China's retail market, Goodale said in a statement.
The review and approval of exporting establishments by Chinese authorities have yet to be finalized.
The criteria for exporting plants should be set this year.

"Any inroads into the vast Chinese beef market can only be good news for Canadian producers. Getting into China before our major trading partners provides a real opportunity for increased sales of Canadian beef," Canadian Cattlemen's Association president Dave Andrews said in Goodale's press release.
